result.question: Before I trust any DGA numbers from Transformer 1 at site MAIN, confirm the transformer is registered at that site. Then compare the sensors assigned to it with the fields that actually show up in its data stream. List any assigned sensor that never reports a value, and for each measured channel give its non-null count and first and last timestamps. Pay particular attention to hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene, co and co2, and tell me which of these have enough data for a fault interpretation, meaning at least 3 non-null samples. If any of those seven gases is assigned but never measured, name it and say which remaining gas can stand in for it. Use hydrogen for acetylene, ethane for methane, and co2 for co.
result.answer:
The DGA data for Transformer 1 is complete: all seven gases have 5 numeric readings each, so no gas needs a stand-in.

**Registration:** Transformer 1 is registered at site MAIN. It's one of 6 assets there, alongside Chiller 6, Motor_01, PUMP3, hyd_1 and mp_1.

**Assigned vs. measured sensors:** 30 sensors are assigned and the same 30 fields appear in the data stream. **No assigned sensor is missing a value.**

**Coverage per measured channel:** The stream has only 5 records, one per day. Every channel has a non-null count of **5**, first timestamp **2024-01-15T00:00:00** and last timestamp **2024-01-19T00:00:00**. All values are numeric with no nulls. The channels are:
acetylene, ati, co, co2, dbds, dielectric_rigidity, ethane, ethylene, hydrogen, il1, il2, il3, interfacial_v, inut, methane, nitrogen, oti, oti_a, oti_t, oxygen, power_factor, rated_mva, vl1, vl12, vl2, vl23, vl3, vl31, water_content, wti.

**The seven fault gases:**

| Gas | Non-null count | Range (min–max) | Enough for interpretation (≥3)? |
|---|---|---|---|
| hydrogen | 5 | 2800–2950 | Yes |
| methane | 5 | 7200–7406 | Yes |
| ethane | 5 | 5400–5500 | Yes |
| ethylene | 5 | 16500–16700 | Yes |
| acetylene | 5 | 6–8 | Yes |
| co | 5 | 30–35 | Yes |
| co2 | 5 | 1300–1350 | Yes |

**Substitutions:** None are needed, because all seven gases are assigned and measured. The hydrogen-for-acetylene, ethane-for-methane and co2-for-co stand-ins don't apply.

**Caveats:**
- The data is 5 daily samples from January 2024, so it's more than two years old.
- The oil temperature alarm flag (`oti_a`) should only be 0 or 1, but it reads up to 2.
- The oil temperature trip flag (`oti_t`) is 1 in every sample.

The gas values are also high enough to deserve attention in the fault interpretation.
